health_zone_table.basis: Printed per-health-zone table of SitRep 093 for 2026-08-15. Fifty-five zone rows plus the province's unventilated CTE-death block. No newly affected health zone; the national footprint holds at 55 of 151.

reconciliation.note: Zone rows sum to 4945 confirmed and 2195 deaths; with the 130-death unventilated block that closes on Ituri's printed province row, and the province column closes exactly on the printed national total. The province column advances +102 cases against 101 printed new, and the edition's own footnote accounts for the difference exactly: a Makiso (Tshopo) case recorded on 14 August was omitted from SitRep 92's cumulative and is restored here, taking Tshopo 11 -> 13 on one printed new case. Deaths advance +53 against 53 printed, closing in every province with no residual.
reconciliation.restatement_scope: tshopo cumulative corrected upward by one case; the edition states a Makiso case recorded 14 August was omitted from SitRep 92's cumulative

lab_indicators_24h.note: This edition publishes per-province sample denominators and positivity rates, which SitReps 90 to 92 did not, but still prints no national rate and none is derived. Ituri: 89 new positives (59 living, 30 deceased) on 288 new samples, 30.9%, plus 8 repeat positives on a further 79 samples. Nord-Kivu 8 confirmed (3 deceased) on 133 samples, 6.0%. Haut-Uele 3 confirmed (all living) on 9 samples, 33.3%. Tshopo 1 confirmed on 6 samples, 16.6%. The provinces use different bases (Ituri separates new from repeat samples; the others do not), so the per-province rates are not a comparable series.

care_continuity: The national isolation/CTE census is 730 patients, but it is not the sum of its published parts: the four provinces that publish a care block total 733 (Ituri 548, Nord-Kivu 170, Tshopo 8, Sud-Kivu 7) and Haut-Uele publishes no care block at all despite 138 cumulative cases.

Ituri reports 548 patients against 991 beds (55.3% occupancy), split 236 confirmed on 497 beds and 312 suspects on 494 beds; the aggregate conceals saturated units at Bambu (confirmed and suspect), Fataki and Nizi (confirmed), plus Aru, Kilo, Logo and Kigonze on the suspect side.

Nord-Kivu reports 170 patients against 206 beds (82.5% occupancy) with suspect-bed occupancy at 100%, and Butembo, Masereka, Vuhovi and Kalunguta suspects isolated in facilities that are not transit centres.
Tshopo holds 8 patients on 12 beds at the Kisangani centre; Sud-Kivu follows 7 suspects at Katana and records 66 days without a new confirmed case since 10 June 2026.
highlights: The DRC headline is 4945 confirmed cases and 2325 confirmed deaths; the country-scope endpoint is 4965 confirmed and 2327 deaths after the separately sourced Uganda 20/2 anchor.
The edition records 101 new confirmed cases in 24 hours: 89 in Ituri, 8 in Nord-Kivu, 3 in Haut-Uele and 1 in Tshopo, with no new affected health zone; the footprint holds at 55 of 151.

The front page reports 33 community deaths while the zone table prints 33 community plus 20 intra-CTE for the same 24 hours, so the day's confirmed-death total is 53 and the front-page figure is the community subset only.
INSP corrects its own prior edition: a Makiso (Tshopo) case recorded on 14 August was omitted from SitRep 92's cumulative, so Tshopo advances 11 to 13 on one printed new case.
Contact follow-up regains the 85% threshold at 85.3% (20791 of 24383), and this is the first edition in this run to publish a per-province contact table.

care_capacity_ituri.note: Ituri only. No national bed inventory is published, so this is never treated as national capacity. The province aggregate conceals saturated units: the Bambu confirmed AND suspect wards, Fataki, and the Nizi confirmed ward, plus Aru, Kilo, Logo and Kigonze on the suspect side.

challenges: Weak alert escalation and incomplete listing and follow-up of contacts around confirmed cases.

Points of entry remain under-operationalised in Tshopo: 7 of 20 sites active (35%) with 57.1% reporting completeness, for want of training, supervision, and logistic and financial support; in Ituri only 1 of 11 strategic sites runs without interruption.
Responders unpaid in Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uele, causing a strike that deprived six Haut-Uele points of entry of reporting entirely.
2187 screening refusals recorded in Nord-Kivu (2.78%), and weak screening at the Pont-Shari post in Ituri for want of uniformed-service involvement.

Infection-prevention delivery short in Ituri: 21 of 171 expected rings opened, 64 of 77 identified sites decontaminated with 13 gaps beyond 48 hours, attributed to insufficient decontamination teams, input shortages, family resistance, unfound addresses, and a decontaminators' strike.
Referral capacity short: 2 ambulances out of service in Ituri, only 5 available in Nord-Kivu, and 10 further ambulances needed in Haut-Uele.

Treatment capacity saturated: the Bambu confirmed and suspect wards, Fataki and the Nizi confirmed ward are full in Ituri; suspect-bed occupancy reaches 100% in Nord-Kivu, where Butembo, Masereka, Vuhovi and Kalunguta suspects are isolated in facilities that are not transit centres; Haut-Uele still has no standard treatment centre in any of its six affected zones; the Kisangani centre holds 12 beds.
Community resistance continues to block safe burial and decontamination, with two failures in Beni and Kalunguta and family resistance recorded in Kilo.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: First edition in this run to publish a per-province contact table; the four published provinces sum exactly to the national figures. Haut-Uele's 61.8% is explicitly incomplete (4 health zones did not report), and Sud-Kivu is absent because it has no active contact.

operational_tables.note: Operational figures are the edition's own printed values. Tshopo's alert row is ND and the province is described as non-reporting, while it simultaneously reports contacts and points-of-entry throughput.

poe_poc_national.coverage_note: Four-province total that INCLUDES Sud-Kivu (84432), which SitRep 91 excluded from its own total, and EXCLUDES Haut-Uele, whose points of entry did not report because responders struck. The basis changes edition to edition, so this is not a travel-volume series.

priorities: Hold contact follow-up above the 85% threshold it has just regained (85.3%), and close the Haut-Uele gap where 4 health zones did not report and coverage stands at 61.8%.
Pay responders: non-payment in Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uele has already struck out six Haut-Uele points of entry and the Ituri decontamination teams.
Relieve the saturated Ituri wards (Bambu, Fataki, Nizi) and Nord-Kivu's 100% suspect-bed occupancy, and establish standard treatment capacity in the six affected Haut-Uele zones.

preserved_conflicts: 24-hour death split: the front-page highlights state '101 newly confirmed cases including 33 (community) deaths', naming only the community component, while the edition's own zone table prints 33 community plus 20 intra-CTE deaths for the same 24 hours, totalling 53. The zone table is internally consistent and closes on every province, so 53 is promoted as the 24-hour confirmed-death figure and the front-page 33 is preserved as the community subset it actually describes. A reader taking the highlights at face value would understate the day's confirmed deaths by 38%.

SitRep 92 cumulative corrected: the province summary carries the footnote that a Makiso (Tshopo) case recorded on 14 August was omitted from SitRep 92's cumulative. Tshopo therefore advances 11 -> 13 on a single printed new case, and the province column advances +102 against 101 printed new. The correction is the source's own and is promoted as printed; SitRep 92's published promotion is left as INSP published it rather than retroactively edited.

isolation census does not sum: the national headline prints 730 patients in isolation/CTE, while the four provinces that publish a care block sum to 733 (Ituri 548, Nord-Kivu 170, Tshopo 8, Sud-Kivu 7) and Haut-Uele publishes no care block at all despite being an affected province with 138 cumulative cases. The national figure is promoted as printed, the published province components are carried, Haut-Uele is recorded as not published, and the three-patient excess is disclosed rather than reconciled.

points-of-entry total: the per-province table sums to 298841 travellers (132493 + 78435 + 84432 + 3481) against a printed global of 298850, a nine-person excess. The printed global is promoted and the excess preserved.

Tshopo reporting status: the surveillance text states Tshopo remains non-reporting and counts only four reporting provinces, and the alert table prints ND across every Tshopo cell. The same edition credits Tshopo with 100% contact follow-up (439/439) and 3481 travellers through its points of entry. The province is simultaneously described as non-reporting and reporting; each figure is carried where the edition prints it and the contradiction is preserved.
SitRep 93 is DRC-only at 4945 confirmed / 2325 deaths; the country-scope snapshot adds the stable Uganda 20/2/11 anchor separately -> 4965 / 2327 / 1051.

review_notes: Official INSP PDF, 10 pages, SHA-256 0697ebde50404f283a1a143d471b2eb12aaf12a3cdc2b1371d516e7041888c2a, 697123 bytes, staged and archived from the INSP WordPress feed (post 25339, media 25340).

Ten-page edition: one page longer than SitReps 90 to 92. The additional length carries a per-province points-of-entry indicator table and a per-province contact-tracing breakdown, neither of which earlier editions in this run published. Zone-table geometry is unchanged and the extractor reconciled it without modification.

No newly affected health zone; the footprint holds at 55 of 151 and the six-province geography is unchanged, so the Bas-Uele and Tshopo zone registrations from SitReps 90 and 91 carry forward untouched.
Contact follow-up regains the 85% threshold at 85.3%, up from 82.6% at SitRep 91, on a larger denominator (24383 under follow-up).
Sud-Kivu records 66 days without a new confirmed case since 10 June 2026.
